speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Finance whether the Ministry will consider releasing a draft Budget Statement for public consultation one month before the delivery of the Budget Statement in Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Throughout the year, the Government gathers feedback and studies data to formulate and implement better plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This consultation effort goes beyond MOF and includes the outreach and consultations by other Ministries and REACH to Singaporeans, businesses, workers and various sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The process is structured along certain themes and questions, which, in a way, reflects some of the areas being examined for the coming Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: REACH also hosted events, such as the Pre-Budget 2017 Conversation and Facebook Q&A Session, for Singaporeans to directly engage with policymakers and Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: MOF ran engagement sessions with stakeholders, such as trade associations and grassroots leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This past year, through the work of the Committee on the Future Economy, there were additional engagement sessions with students, industry leaders, unionists and academics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Feedback received during these consultations had further contributed to the formulation of the Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The current spread of engagement opportunities during the year, growing more intensive nearer Budget Day, achieves the goal of engaging Singaporeans to think about our future, as Mr Louis Ng's suggestion intends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Budget is not a destination, but part of a journey of feedback-gathering, analysis, policy review and refinement, in order to improve Singapore and the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, at least they can give feedback, meaningful ones which we can use to amend or improve the Budget.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because what we are doing now in a lot of our dialogues is explaining the Budget to people and we are not really getting their feedback on how we can improve it further.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are really two parts to the consultation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The explaining part comes after the Budget has been delivered.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Prior to that, there is a great deal of consultations and the consultations take place not just in the month or two before the Budget Statement is delivered, but it sometimes takes a long time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It was two years in the making from feedback from people about their concerns and also the feedback that they wanted to honour the elderly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This was something that was borne out of the CFE discussions and recommendations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, prior to the Budget, there were a lot of consultations, some of which were years in the making, some of which were in that year itself, some of it were in the months prior, or a month or two before.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, on elder care, how we can assist for an ageing population.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These are themes that we float and discuss with people, and then we put them into the Budget.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because whatever it is, in any Budget Statement, there will always be different views.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, if we were to put up a Budget and say, "We want to raise worker levies", what do you think the response would be?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There would be some who may say, "Yes, let us do it straightaway".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I suspect there would be a lot more who would say "no".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we draw in ideas from the consultations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Parliament comes back and gives its final input and suggestions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is why the Motion that is moved by the Minister for Finance, when we have the Budget debates, is that "this Parliament approves the fiscal policy of the Government".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the process is really designed to be as efficient as possible but, at the same time, taking on broad feedback, and to the extent that it is not possible to incorporate something in a particular financial year but if it is a good idea, we will see if we can incorporate it in the months ahead, or in the following year.
